q-277948.name: Question 1
q-277948.problem: The horizontal asymptote of the function $f(x)=\frac{7x-9{x}^{2}}{3{x}^{2}+8x-5}$ is $y=${{field-1}}.
q-277948.worked_solution:
To find the horizontal asymptote of a rational function, we divide every term in the numerator and denominator by the dominant term in the denominator, and then we let $x\to \infty .$

In this case, the dominant term in the denominator is ${x}^{2}.$ So, we divide every term in the numerator and denominator by ${x}^{2},$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x) & =\frac{7x-9{x}^{2}}{3{x}^{2}+8x-5} \\  & =\frac{(\frac{7x}{{x}^{2}}-\frac{9{x}^{2}}{{x}^{2}})}{(\frac{3{x}^{2}}{{x}^{2}}+\frac{8x}{{x}^{2}}-\frac{5}{{x}^{2}})} \\  & =\frac{(\frac{7}{x}-9)}{(3+\frac{8}{x}-\frac{5}{{x}^{2}})}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, when $x$ is very large, the terms $\frac{7}{x},$ $\frac{8}{x},$ and $\frac{5}{{x}^{2}}$ become very small. Therefore, as $x\to \infty ,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x) & =\frac{(\frac{7}{x}-9)}{(3+\frac{8}{x}-\frac{5}{{x}^{2}})} \\  & \to \frac{0-9}{3+0-0} \\  & =-3.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the horizontal asymptote is $y=-3.$

q-277952.name: Question 2
q-277952.problem: The horizontal asymptote of the function $f(x)=\frac{3x(4{x}^{2}+7)}{6{x}^{3}-5{x}^{2}}$ is $y=${{field-1}}.
q-277952.worked_solution:
The given function can be rewritten as follows:

$$
f(x)=\frac{12{x}^{3}+21x}{6{x}^{3}-5{x}^{2}}
$$

To find the horizontal asymptote of a rational function, we divide every term in the numerator and denominator by the dominant term in the denominator, and then we let $x\to \infty .$

Ignoring the coefficient, the dominant term in the denominator is ${x}^{3}.$ So, we divide every term in the numerator and denominator by ${x}^{3},$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x) & =\frac{12{x}^{3}+21x}{6{x}^{3}-5{x}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{(\frac{12{x}^{3}}{{x}^{3}}+\frac{21x}{{x}^{3}})}{(\frac{6{x}^{3}}{{x}^{3}}-\frac{5{x}^{2}}{{x}^{3}})} \\  & =\frac{(12+\frac{21}{{x}^{2}})}{(6-\frac{5}{x})}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, when $x$ is very large, the terms $\frac{21}{{x}^{2}}$ and $\frac{5}{x}$ become very small. Therefore, as $x\to \infty ,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x) & =\frac{(12+\frac{21}{{x}^{2}})}{(6-\frac{5}{x})} \\  & \to \frac{12+0}{6-0} \\  & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the horizontal asymptote is $y=2.$

q-6885.name: Question 3
q-6885.problem: Determine the horizontal asymptote of the function $f(x)=\frac{5{x}^{2}+2}{{x}^{4}-1}.$
q-6885.worked_solution:
To find the horizontal asymptote of a rational function, we divide every term in the numerator and denominator by the dominant term in the denominator, and then we let $x\to \infty .$

Ignoring the coefficient, the dominant term in the denominator is ${x}^{4}.$ So, we divide every term in the numerator and denominator by ${x}^{4},$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x) & =\frac{5{x}^{2}+2}{{x}^{4}-1} \\  & =\frac{(\frac{5{x}^{2}}{{x}^{4}}+\frac{2}{{x}^{4}})}{(\frac{{x}^{4}}{{x}^{4}}-\frac{1}{{x}^{4}})} \\  & =\frac{(\frac{5}{{x}^{2}}+\frac{2}{{x}^{4}})}{(1-\frac{1}{{x}^{4}})}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, when $x$ is very large, the terms $\frac{5}{{x}^{2}},\frac{2}{{x}^{4}}$ and $\frac{1}{{x}^{4}}$ become very small. Therefore, as $x\to \infty ,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x) & =\frac{(\frac{5}{{x}^{2}}+\frac{2}{{x}^{4}})}{(1-\frac{1}{{x}^{4}})} \\  & \to \frac{0+0}{1-0} \\  & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the horizontal asymptote is $y=0.$

Determine the horizontal asymptote of the function f(x)=5x2+2x4−1.

a
y=1
b
y=2
c
y=0
d
y=5
e
No horizontal asymptote.
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

To find the horizontal asymptote of a rational function, we divide every term in the numerator and denominator by the dominant term in the denominator, and then we let x→∞.

Ignoring the coefficient, the dominant term in the denominator is x4. So, we divide every term in the numerator and denominator by x4, as follows:

f(x)=5x2+2x4−1=(5x2x4+2x4)(x4x4−1x4)=(5x2+2x4)(1−1x4)

Now, when x is very large, the terms 5x2,2x4 and 1x4 become very small. Therefore, as x→∞, we have

f(x)=(5x2+2x4)(1−1x4)→0+01−0=0.

So, the horizontal asymptote is y=0.

q-4002.name: Question 4
q-4002.problem: Determine the horizontal asymptote of the function $f(x)=\frac{x+5}{{x}^{2}-x-2}.$
q-4002.worked_solution:
To find the horizontal asymptote of a rational function, we divide every term in the numerator and denominator by the dominant term in the denominator, and then we let $x\to \infty .$

Ignoring the coefficient, the dominant term in the denominator is ${x}^{2}.$ So, we divide every term in the numerator and denominator by ${x}^{2},$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x) & =\frac{x+5}{{x}^{2}-x-2} \\  & =\frac{(\frac{x}{{x}^{2}}+\frac{5}{{x}^{2}})}{(\frac{{x}^{2}}{{x}^{2}}-\frac{x}{{x}^{2}}-\frac{2}{{x}^{2}})} \\  & =\frac{(\frac{1}{x}+\frac{5}{{x}^{2}})}{(1-\frac{1}{x}-\frac{2}{{x}^{2}})}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, when $x$ is very large, the terms $\frac{1}{x},\frac{5}{{x}^{2}}$ and $\frac{2}{{x}^{2}}$ become very small. Therefore, as $x\to \infty ,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x) & =\frac{(\frac{1}{x}+\frac{5}{{x}^{2}})}{(1-\frac{1}{x}-\frac{2}{{x}^{2}})} \\  & \to \frac{0+0}{1-0-0} \\  & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the horizontal asymptote is $y=0.$

Question 4
?

Determine the horizontal asymptote of the function f(x)=x+5x2−x−2.

a
y=0
b
y=52
c
No horizontal asymptotes
d
y=−52
e
y=−1,2
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

To find the horizontal asymptote of a rational function, we divide every term in the numerator and denominator by the dominant term in the denominator, and then we let x→∞.

Ignoring the coefficient, the dominant term in the denominator is x2. So, we divide every term in the numerator and denominator by x2, as follows:

f(x)=x+5x2−x−2=(xx2+5x2)(x2x2−xx2−2x2)=(1x+5x2)(1−1x−2x2)

Now, when x is very large, the terms 1x,5x2 and 2x2 become very small. Therefore, as x→∞, we have

f(x)=(1x+5x2)(1−1x−2x2)→0+01−0−0=0.

So, the horizontal asymptote is y=0.

q-6994.name: Question 5
q-6994.worked_solution:
The given function can be rewritten as follows:

$$
f(x)=\frac{10-3x-{x}^{2}}{17x+7}
$$

To find the horizontal asymptote of a rational function, we divide every term in the numerator and denominator by the dominant term in the denominator, and then we let $x\to \infty .$

Ignoring the coefficient, the dominant term in the denominator is $x.$ So, we divide every term in the numerator and denominator by $x,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x) & =\frac{10-3x-{x}^{2}}{17x+7} \\  & =\frac{(\frac{10}{x}-\frac{3x}{x}-\frac{{x}^{2}}{x})}{(\frac{17x}{x}+\frac{7}{x})} \\  & =\frac{(\frac{10}{x}-3-x)}{(17+\frac{7}{x})}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, when $x$ is very large, the terms $\frac{10}{x}$ and $\frac{7}{x}$ become very small. Therefore, as $x\to \infty ,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x) & =\frac{(\frac{10}{x}-3-x)}{(17+\frac{7}{x})} \\  & ≈\frac{0-3-x}{17+0} \\  & =-\frac{x+3}{17}.\end{aligned}
$$

This is not a constant, which means that $y=f(x)$ does not have a horizontal asymptote.

q-113180.worked_solution:
To find the horizontal asymptote of a rational function, we divide every term in the numerator and denominator by the dominant term in the denominator, and then we let $x\to \infty .$

Ignoring the coefficient, the dominant term in the denominator is $x.$ So, we divide every term in the numerator and denominator by $x,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x) & =\frac{{x}^{3}}{3x+2} \\  & =\frac{(\frac{{x}^{3}}{x})}{(\frac{3x}{x}+\frac{2}{x})} \\  & =\frac{{x}^{2}}{(3+\frac{2}{x})}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, when $x$ is very large, the term $\frac{2}{x}$ becomes very small. Therefore, as $x\to \infty ,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x) & =\frac{{x}^{2}}{(3+\frac{2}{x})} \\  & ≈\frac{{x}^{2}}{3+0} \\  & =\frac{1}{3}{x}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

This is not a constant, which means that $y=f(x)$ does not have a horizontal asymptote.
